  44:     """Wrap a Version binary op method in a type-check."""

  46:     @wraps(operator)

  48:         cls = type(self)
  49:         comparable_types = (

  51:             dict,
  52:             tuple,
  53:             list,
  54:             *String.__args__,  # type: ignore

  56:         if not isinstance(other, comparable_types):
  57:             return NotImplemented
  58:         if isinstance(other, (dict, tuple, list)):
  59:             # A collection that cannot construct a comparable version is
  60:             # not a valid comparison operand.  Return NotImplemented
  61:             # instead of leaking conversion errors from __init__.

  76: class Version:

  79:

  82:     :param major: version when you make incompatible API changes.
  83:     :param minor: version when you add functionality in a backwards-compatible manner.

  86:     :param build: an optional build string
  87:     """

  95:     _LAST_NUMBER: ClassVar[Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"(?:[^\d]*(\d+)[^\d]*)+")

  97:     _LAST_PRERELEASE: ClassVar[Pattern[str]] = re.compile(r"^(.*\.)?(\d+)$")

 101:     )

 105:     )

 108:         str
 109:     ] = rf"""

 111:             (?P<major>0|[1-9]\d*)
 112:             (?:
 113:                 \.

 115:                 (?:

 118:                 ){{opt_patch}}

 120:             (?:-(?P<prerelease>
 121:                 (?:{_PRERELEASE_IDENTIFIER.pattern})
 122:                 (?:\.(?:{_PRERELEASE_IDENTIFIER.pattern}))*
 123:             ))?
 124:             (?:\+(?P<build>
 125:                 (?:{_BUILD_IDENTIFIER.pattern})
 126:                 (?:\.(?:{_BUILD_IDENTIFIER.pattern}))*
 127:             ))?
 128:             \Z
 129:         """
 130:     #: Regex for a semver version
 131:     _REGEX: ClassVar[Pattern[str]] = re.compile(
 132:         _REGEX_TEMPLATE.format(opt_patch="", opt_minor=""),
 133:         re.VERBOSE | re.ASCII,
 134:     )
 135:     #: Regex for a semver version that might be shorter
 136:     _REGEX_OPTIONAL_MINOR_AND_PATCH: ClassVar[Pattern[str]] = re.compile(
 137:         _REGEX_TEMPLATE.format(opt_patch="?", opt_minor="?"),
 138:         re.VERBOSE | re.ASCII,
 139:     )

 141:     def __init__(
 142:         self,
 143:         major: SupportsInt,
 144:         minor: SupportsInt = 0,
 145:         patch: SupportsInt = 0,
 146:         prerelease: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None,
 147:         build: Optional[Union[String, int]] = None,
 148:     ):

 150:         version_parts = {"major": int(major), "minor": int(minor), "patch": int(patch)}
 151: 
 152:         for name, value in version_parts.items():
 153:             if value < 0:
 154:                 raise ValueError(
 155:                     "{!r} is negative. A version can only be positive.".format(name)
 156:                 )

 158:         self._major = version_parts["major"]

 160:         self._patch = version_parts["patch"]
 161:         self._prerelease = None if prerelease is None else str(prerelease)
 162:         self._build = None if build is None else str(build)

 164:     @classmethod
 165:     def _validate_identifiers(
 166:         cls, value: str, pattern: Pattern[str], what: str
 167:     ) -> None:

 170:         identifiers allowed by the SemVer grammar.

 172:         :param value: the identifier string to check
 173:         :param pattern: the regex a single identifier must match
 174:         :param what: human readable name of the checked part,
 175:             used for the error message
 176:         :raises ValueError: if any dot-separated part is not a valid identifier
 177:         """
 178:         for identifier in value.split("."):
 179:             if not pattern.fullmatch(identifier):
 180:                 raise ValueError(
 181:                     f"{value!r} is not a valid {what}. It may only consist of "
 182:                     "dot-separated identifiers, made of alphanumerics and "
 183:                     "hyphens."
 184:                 )

 199:         b_parts = [int(x) if x.isdigit() else x for x in (b or "").split(".")]
